caveats: Embedded official catalog provides per-minute EUR ex-VAT rates and regional shapes. USD equivalents use ECB September 28, 2026 reference 1 EUR = 1.1378 USD; invoice is still EUR and bank FX/spreads may differ. native_node_hour=exact perMinute×60. Approximate monthly display is not a contractual cap.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

Multi-GPU SKUs (2/4/8 GPUs) priced per GPU with gpu_min_count = N (sold only as N-GPU instances); the 'alt' flag was removed (ordinary GPU VMs, not an adjacent product). Per-GPU rates from the page __NEXT_DATA__ per-minute catalog (research/providers/scaleway-gpu.json, 2026-09-28); live page check: L4-2/4/8 EUR 1.58/3.15/6.30 per hour = 2/4/8 x L4-1 EUR 0.79.

Block storage: Block Storage 5K EUR 0.000130/GB-h (~EUR 0.0949/GB-month, disk_gib_month converted at 1.1378) billed while the volume exists; 15K tier EUR 0.000177/GB-h; Block/Unified Snapshot EUR 0.000049/GB-h (scaleway.com/en/pricing/storage, 2026-09-28). GPU instances list "Block storage" (+ free scratch NVMe on L40S/H100/B300) with no included boot volume, so included_disk_gib 0.

Egress: the GPU pricing page publishes no egress charge; Scaleway Virtual Instances say "List prices include egress and IPv6" but the GPU page does not repeat it, so egress_gib stays null (unverified, not free). Flexible IPv4 EUR 0.005/h (scaleway.com/en/pricing/network).

Structure 2026-09-28: the catalog listed each SKU once per availability zone (fr-par-1/fr-par-2/pl-waw-2) at the same price; duplicates merged into one regime per SKU, label names the zones. Removed keys: on-demand-h100-2-80g-h100-pcie-5, on-demand-h100-1-80g-h100-pcie-7, on-demand-l40s-8-48g-l40s-9, on-demand-l40s-4-48g-l40s-11, on-demand-l40s-2-48g-l40s-13, on-demand-l40s-1-48g-l40s-15, on-demand-l4-8-24g-l4-17, on-demand-l4-8-24g-l4-18, on-demand-l4-4-24g-l4-20, on-demand-l4-4-24g-l4-21, on-demand-l4-2-24g-l4-23, on-demand-l4-2-24g-l4-24, on-demand-l4-1-24g-l4-26, on-demand-l4-1-24g-l4-27.

Every GPU Instance needs a block boot volume (min 10 GB, 125 GB recommended for GPU OS): 125 GB x EUR 0.000130/GB-h = ~EUR 11.9 (~$13.5)/month while the volume exists, billed even when powered off. A flexible IPv4 (EUR 0.005/h) is created by default unless unticked.
No commitment discount exists for GPU Instances: Compute Savings Plans (up to 25%) exclude B300, H100, RENDER, L4, L40S. Only on-demand pricing (or Elastic Metal monthly / sales contracts).
Standby (stop-in-place) bills full compute; only 'power off' (archive) stops GPU billing. Kapsule GPU node pools are billed from creation, including GPU-operator setup time.

Scaleway Billing FAQ says each Instance resource is "billed separately for a minimum of 60 minutes" per start/stop period, while the Instances FAQ says GPU Instances are "billed per minute of uptime". The 60-minute minimum is not confirmed for GPU Instances; if it applies, sessions under 1 h cost up to ~6x the per-minute estimate.

fleet.verification: Validated payment method plus identity verification; higher-end/multi-GPU shapes require support.
fleet.tiers: Payment-only accounts cannot use GPU Instances. Identity unlocks 1 RENDER-S, L4-1 or L40S-1 per listed shape; H100/multi-GPU shapes need support.
fleet.notes: Zero describes before identity verification; not a claim of zero after verified onboarding. Higher limits require human review.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Scratch storage does not survive once the server is stopped: doing a full stop/start cycle will erase the scratch data.
snapshot_auto.note: No automatic snapshot on stop. Block Storage volumes simply persist (persistent_disk); legacy local volumes are moved to a volume store in Power-off mode (disk persistence, not a snapshot); GPU scratch NVMe is erased on full stop; no memory state kept.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: An image is a complete backup of your Instance. One image contains all the volumes of your Instance and can be used to restore your Instance and its data. You can also use it to create a series of Instances with a predefined configuration.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Per-volume Block Storage snapshots or whole-Instance images (console/CLI/API); new Instances can boot from images; disk only, no memory; scratch storage excluded ("does not support features like snapshots").

harness_api.quote: Launch powerful cloud GPU instances for AI, ML, and rendering.
harness_api.note: Scaleway GPU Instances are plain IaaS GPU VMs (bring-your-own-OS-image compute, billed per minute) with no first-party API to drive a coding agent harness (prompt/stream events/follow-ups); no such product is mentioned anywhere in the GPU docs or marketing pages. Outside product scope, like Windows on a Linux-only sandbox API.

egress_allowlist.quote: You can create customized inbound and outbound rules to drop or accept traffic on particular protocols, ports, and IP ranges.
egress_allowlist.note: Security groups with default outbound policy drop/accept ("You can set default policies to drop or accept all inbound traffic, and drop or accept all outbound traffic."); enforced outside the VM on public traffic. No domain/FQDN rules documented.

ingress_rules.quote: We recommend blocking incoming traffic by default to prevent intrusions.
ingress_rules.note: Security-group inbound rules by protocol/port/IP range; Instances can also sit on Private Networks without a public IP (via Public Gateway).

guest_firewall.note: Full VM with root (Ubuntu GPU OS images); nftables/iptables inside should work.

secret_proxy.quote: Secret Manager is a solution that provides a centralized location where your secrets can be stored and accessed.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are fetched into the machine (Secret Manager API / env / cloud-init); no credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: You can attach up to 15 volumes at a time to a single Instance.
volume_attach.note: Block Storage volumes (5K/15K IOPS) in the same AZ.

volume_shared.quote: Currently, only Linux-based POP2, BASIC3-X, STANDARD2-A, STANDARD3-X CPU Instances, L4, L40S, and H100 GPU Instances are fully qualified for File Storage.
volume_shared.note: Scaleway File Storage: network file system shared read-write by several Instances in the same region ("File systems can be shared by several Instances"); B300/RENDER-S not listed as qualified.

isolation.note: Scaleway Instances (including GPU Instances) run as guest VMs under a QEMU/KVM hypervisor; docs reference 'QEMU Guest Agent' and 'the underlying hypervisor' for Local/scratch storage. No lower-level microVM tech (Firecracker/cloud-hypervisor) documented for this product.

image_oci.quote: select an operating system image suitable for your GPU Instance. For example, select Ubuntu Noble GPU OS 13 (NVIDIA), which comes with preinstalled NVIDIA drivers and an NVIDIA Docker environment.
image_oci.note: not offered: GPU Instances boot from VM disk images (Scaleway OS images / custom images from snapshots), not from a Docker/OCI image; Docker containers can be run inside the VM once booted, but that is not the same as starting the machine from an OCI image.

desktop.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (headless GPU compute VM; no managed VNC/RDP desktop stream product exists for GPU Instances).

browser.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (raw GPU compute VM; no managed/preinstalled browser product).

computer_use.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no screenshot/click desktop-driving API for a GPU compute VM).

anti_bot.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (plain GPU cloud VM, no stealth/fingerprinting browser-automation feature).

captcha_solving.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU cloud compute, not a browser/scraping product).

egress_ip_type.note: A datacenter-range Flexible IPv4 is attached to the Instance (created by default unless unticked) and persists with the resource/account; it is a fixed, allocatable/detachable datacenter IP, not residential/mobile or rotating.

fork.quote: An image is a complete backup of your Instance. ... You can also use it to create a series of Instances with a predefined configuration.
fork.note: Instance images (whole-Instance backups) can be used to launch new Instances cloned from an existing one; this is disk/fs-based cloning of a (typically stopped) machine, not a running-memory fork.

fork_running.quote: An image is a complete backup of your Instance. One image contains all the volumes of your Instance and can be used to restore your Instance and its data.
fork_running.note: Image/snapshot creation is disk-based; no documented ability to clone a running Instance's memory state without stopping/quiescing it first.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Scratch storage does not survive once the server is stopped: doing a full stop/start cycle will erase the scratch data.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots/images are filesystem/disk only (snapshot=fs in the card); no memory-state capture, so forked clones cannot resume running processes.

wake_on_request.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; GPU Instances are manually started/stopped IaaS VMs with no request-triggered autowake mechanism documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Which options are available to power off my Instance?
auto_stop_idle.note: Power-off/standby are user- or API-triggered actions; no documented idle-detection auto-stop feature for GPU Instances (unlike serverless/sandbox platforms).

live_resize.quote: Can I resize my Instance? Yes, you can resize (also called vertical scaling) your Instance to adjust CPU, RAM, and storage capacity without having to recreate it.
live_resize.note: Resizing (changing commercial type) does not require recreating the Instance, but is not documented as being applied to a live/running machine without a stop; standard Scaleway resize workflow powers the Instance off first.

agent_harnesses.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) templates or preinstall offered for GPU Instances.

own_agent_api.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Scaleway has no first-party browser/computer-use task-agent API for GPU Instances.

mcp_server.note: Scaleway's public GitHub org has no dedicated MCP server product for driving Instances/GPU sandboxes as of this check; only an unrelated 'scaleway-skills' repo was found.

lang_python.quote: select an operating system image suitable for your GPU Instance. For example, select Ubuntu Noble GPU OS 13 (NVIDIA), which comes with preinstalled NVIDIA drivers and an NVIDIA Docker environment.
lang_python.note: GPU OS images are Ubuntu-based and include a preinstalled ML environment (docs reference 'Use the preinstalled environment' and Pipenv virtual environments), which includes Python by default.

inbound_https.quote: You can create customized inbound and outbound rules to drop or accept traffic on particular protocols, ports, and IP ranges.
inbound_https.note: not offered: this is a raw IaaS VM with a public IPv4/security groups, not a managed HTTPS-URL ingress product; any HTTPS endpoint must be self-hosted (e.g. your own nginx) on the raw IP/port.

egress_http_rules.quote: You can set default policies to drop or accept all inbound traffic, and drop or accept all outbound traffic.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is via security groups at IP/port/protocol level only; no documented HTTP method/path level egress rules.

static_egress_ip.note: The Flexible IPv4 attached to the Instance is a fixed, persistent public IP (detachable/reattachable by the customer, not rotated by Scaleway), used for both inbound and outbound traffic.

windows.quote: select an operating system image suitable for your GPU Instance. For example, select Ubuntu Noble GPU OS 13 (NVIDIA), which comes with preinstalled NVIDIA drivers and an NVIDIA Docker environment.
windows.note: not offered: GPU Instance OS images documented are Linux (Ubuntu GPU OS) only; Windows Server images are offered for general-purpose Instances but not documented for the GPU line.

macos.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; macOS is only offered on Scaleway's separate Apple silicon Mac mini product, not GPU Instances.

self_host.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; this is Scaleway's own hosted IaaS on Scaleway datacenters, not software you deploy on your own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Scaleway runs GPU Instances in its own EU datacenters (fr-par, pl-waw), not deployed into the customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: GPU Instances: powerful, secure, and easy-to-use bare metal and virtual GPU servers designed for AI/ML training, inference, and rendering workloads.
open_source.note: not offered: the core GPU Instances platform/control plane is closed-source proprietary Scaleway infrastructure, not released under an OSI license.

sso.quote: Single Sign-On (SSO) allows you to use your Google, Microsoft, or Github account to log in to the console.
sso.note: Scaleway also documents organization-level identity federation / SAML-style SSO setup guides (e.g. 'Set up SSO with Authentik', 'Configure SCIM for Microsoft Entra ID').

max_session_h.quote: GPU Instances ... billed per minute of uptime
max_session_h.note: GPU Instances are full VMs billed per minute of uptime with no documented maximum runtime; they run until the customer stops/deletes them (per-minute billing implies no forced session cutoff).

arm64.quote: CPU Type Intel® Xeon® 6776P (2.3 GHz) ... CPU Type AMD EPYC™ 9334 (2.7GHz) ... CPU Type Xeon Platinum 8452Y (2.0 GHz) ... CPU Type AMD EPYC™ 7413 (2.65GHz) ... CPU Type Dual Intel® Xeon® Platinum 8480C Processors (3.8 GHz)
arm64.note: Every GPU Instance shape (B300, H100 SXM/PCIe, L40S, L4) lists an x86 host CPU (Intel Xeon or AMD EPYC); no ARM64 option exists for GPU Instances. Scaleway does sell separate ARM64 general-purpose Instances (COPARM1/Ampere Altra, e.g. basic2/standard2 SKUs seen in the general Instance catalog), but those are a different, non-GPU product line, so arm64:false is correct for this GPU-cloud card.

nested_virt.note: derived: GPU Instances run as guest VMs under a QEMU/KVM hypervisor (isolation=qemu-kvm); Scaleway's Instances/GPU docs and shared-responsibility/FAQ pages document the hypervisor and virtualization security as Scaleway-managed but never mention exposing VMX/nested-KVM to the guest or a /dev/kvm-in-guest feature for any Instance or GPU Instance type. No documentation found enabling nested virtualization inside the VM.

lang_node.quote: This gives you access to a preinstalled Python environment managed with pipenv. Several useful AI core packages and tools are installed, including scipy, numpy, scikit-learn, jupyter, tensorflow, and the Scaleway SDK.
lang_node.note: The GPU OS images' documented preinstalled environment (conda / pipenv) is Python-specific; no Node.js runtime, npm, or SDK code-exec is documented as preinstalled on GPU Instances. Node.js could be manually installed (root/apt on a generic Ubuntu VM) but that is not 'out of the box'.

soc2.quote: Certifications and qualifications ... ISO/IEC 27001:2022 ... HDS ... SecNumCloud (ongoing)
soc2.note: Scaleway's own Security and Compliance page lists its certifications/qualifications explicitly (ISO/IEC 27001:2022, HDS health-data hosting, SecNumCloud in progress) and does not mention SOC 2 anywhere on this page or elsewhere in the docs found; Scaleway is a French/EU-sovereignty-focused provider whose published attestations are EU-centric, with no SOC 2 report referenced.

hipaa.quote: HDS Health data requires uncompromising security. Scaleway is HDS-certified for the hosting of health data, enabling e-health start-ups, hospitals and medical...
hipaa.note: Scaleway's health-data compliance offering is the French HDS (Hébergeur de Données de Santé) certification, not the US HIPAA framework; no HIPAA-eligibility or BAA is mentioned anywhere on the Security and Compliance page or elsewhere in Scaleway's docs found.

usage_api.quote: Run the following command to obtain your consumption for a specific project only: curl -X GET ... https://api.scaleway.com/billing/v2beta1/consumptions?project_id=SCW_PROJECT_ID
usage_api.note: granularity: per-project; cost: no; Scaleway's Billing API provides consumption data aggregated by project or organization, not per individual GPU Instance. The /billing/v2beta1/consumptions endpoint supports filtering by project_id, category_name, and billing_period, but not by instance ID, tag, or label. Usage is reported as a total per project, not broken down to the per-instance/per-machine level needed to bill individual sandboxes.

locations_quote: Same SKU and price in every listed zone (fr-par-1, fr-par-2, pl-waw-2); per-zone duplicate regimes merged. Availability zones fr-par-1, fr-par-2, pl-waw-2.
